# Checkpoint 1: initial report and menu at the report/menu boundary

**Commands and helpers.** None run here. The entry starts after the pre-menu refresh, step 3 Verify, step 4 Review and step 5 integration, so no `gh`, `git` or helper dispatch happens before this render. The digest names no `--rebase`, so step 2b and its sync review never ran.

**Tracker.**
- `init` ran earlier with `gather, provision, verify`; all three are closed.
- `review` and `report` were added when each started and are closed.
- `menu` is added now as this render starts.

**SHA assessed.** Verification and the brief both assess the digest's assessed `headRefOid`. No push has moved it.

**Template selection.**
- This is the first report, it is not ready, and the course is unset.
- No undispositionable `BLOCKED` exists, so the initial template applies.
- It is the human's own PR, so `deliver` is recommended.
- `deliver with nits` renders because one nit exists.
- The nit footer is omitted because `fix nits` does not render on the initial template.
- No sync line renders because `--rebase` was not passed.

The rendered report follows. The `Verdict:` and `Pick one:` prose lines separate the blocker list from the menu, so the menu does not renumber.

---

Delivers: the reports page exports CSV on demand.

PR comments:
- maria's comment on the missing CSV header is already addressed, so the drafted reply points her at the fix. (src/api/export.ts)

Nits:
- The export pages results with its own loop instead of the shared paging helper, so a paging bug fixed once would need fixing twice. (src/api/export.ts:31, lib/page.ts)

Blockers:
1. The export endpoint ships with no test, so nothing proves it works and nothing catches it breaking. (src/api/export.ts:10-58)
2. The export guide still says exports run nightly while the PR makes them on demand, so a reader following the docs waits for a job that no longer exists. (docs/exports.rst:88)
3. The export ignores the requested date range and returns every row, so a user asking for one month gets the whole history. (src/api/export.ts:60)

Verdict: fixable - 3 blockers

Pick one:
1. assess - post the review to the PR; then deliver or stop, no repairs.
2. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on the base branch, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
3. deliver with nits - deliver, and fold the 1 nit into the repairs.
4. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Course holds until the final menu; `show evidence` prints the full record.

---

# Checkpoint 2: numeric reply `6` on the renumbered final menu

**1. Mapping the reply.**
- Before numeric lookup, `6` matches none of the exact typed commands (`show evidence`, `reply <n>`, `check ...`).
- The menu has N = 4 options: merge, fix nits, reply, stop.
- The adjoining ordered run has L = 3 resolved findings.
- 6 is greater than N, and 6 - 3 = 3 falls within 1-4, so the reply maps to raw option 3, `reply`.
- The menu-layout rule requires an echo before acting. I echo:

  `Taking 6 as option 3 - reply: post the drafted reply to maria's CSV-header comment.`

**2. Freshness check before the external write.**
- I run `gh pr view <N> --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`.
- The head, body and state are unchanged.
- The live `baseRefName` matches `consent.target`.
- The run record validates.

**3. Output done-check.** I re-read the drafted reply against the wording rules and any `## comms style` rules. It passes: ASCII only, no scaffolding, and it ends on the pointer to the fix.

**4. Posting the reply.** I run `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments/<C1 comment id>/replies -f body=<drafted reply>`.
- The post succeeds.
- I record the returned comment id as gate-posted, so the next re-render never mints a `C#` for it.
- I mark C1's reply as posted.

**5. Re-entry.** The post is not a repair selection. The course is unchanged, no wave dispatches, and the round and sync counters stay at 0/6. The head did not move, so the loop re-enters step 5 through the pre-menu refresh.

I stop here, at the post's success. The re-rendered final menu that follows will meet two conditions:
- It drops the `reply` row, because no drafted reply remains.
- It opens with a prose `Pick one:` line, so it cannot adjoin a preceding ordered list again.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## Checkpoint 1

This entry starts at the report/menu boundary. I retain the existing run record and counters; I do not initialize another tracker, run verification, or dispatch a helper. No SHA is newly assessed, and no `Sync:` line renders.

Delivers: the export endpoint produces CSV with the requested date range.

Nits:
- The export endpoint duplicates the shared paging helper, so a paging fix would need to be maintained twice. (src/api/export.ts)

Blockers:
1. The export endpoint has no test, so its CSV behavior is not protected against regressions. (src/api/export.ts:10-58)
2. The export guide says exports run nightly even though they are on demand, so readers wait for a job that does not exist. (docs/exports.rst:88)
3. The export endpoint ignores the requested date range, so the CSV includes records outside the requested period. (src/api/export.ts:60)

Verdict: fixable - 3 blockers

Pick one:
1. assess - post the review to the PR, then offer terminal actions without repairs.
2. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, and watch CI until readiness or an obstacle. [recommended]
3. deliver with nits - deliver, and include the duplicate-paging nit in the repairs.
4. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged.

Course holds until the final menu; `show evidence` prints the full record.

## Independent checkpoint 2

Taking 6 as option 3 - reply; post the drafted reply to maria about the CSV header.

The prior contiguous ordered run contributes three items. There are four raw options, so `6 - 3 = 3` selects reply, not fix nits.

I execute the following simulated sequence, using the existing run record's PR, repository, comment ID, and drafted reply:

- Validate the existing run record and retain the unset course and existing accounting.
- Run `gh pr view <N> -R <base-owner>/<base-repo> --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`. Freshness passes against the stored target, assessed head, and body.
- Apply the output done-check to maria's existing drafted reply. It passes; I do not compose a replacement.
- Run `gh api --method POST repos/<base-owner>/<base-repo>/pulls/<N>/comments/<maria-comment-id>/replies -f body='<existing drafted reply>'`. The simulated post succeeds.
- Persist the returned comment ID as gate-posted so later reconciliation does not mint another comment-ledger entry for it.

No helper is dispatched, no repair selection is created, and neither usage counter changes. This checkpoint stops after the successful reply post.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both facts hold in both outputs, so nothing moved. In Checkpoint 1, Before separates the 1-3 blocker list from the 1-4 menu with the prose `Verdict:` line and keeps evidence in the trailing hint; After does the same and adds a second prose separator (`Pick one:`) plus a hint line naming `show evidence`, so the separation is even more explicit, rows still start at 1, and no numeric evidence row appears. In Checkpoint 2 both outputs compute N=4, L=3, R-L=3, resolve to raw option 3 `reply`, echo the resolution before the freshness check and post, and record no repair grant or wave. The only drift worth noting in After is cosmetic: the stop row text ('remove the worktree') and the `(src/api/export.ts:31, lib/page.ts)` nit locator are not in the entry, and the `---` rules bracketing the rendered report could be read as part of the report; keeping the rendered block free of extra horizontal rules and sticking to the entry's `stop - leave the PR as-is` wording would keep After tight while still delivering the shared-template menu and course-persistence note.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before failed layout because it refused to render the initial menu at all (it treated assess/deliver/deliver-with-nits as forbidden verbs and demanded a numeric show-evidence row), so no four-row list existed to check. After fixes this: the three blockers are an ordered list starting at 1, the "Verdict:" and "Pick one:" paragraphs sit between that list and the four-row menu so Markdown will not renumber the options, the options start at 1 with exactly one [recommended] and stop last, and `show evidence` appears only as a trailing hint sentence. Mapped-pick was already satisfied in Before and survives in After: both echo "Taking 6 as option 3 - reply" with the consequence before the simulated post, dispatch no helper or repair selection, and do not re-ask. The only wording to keep an eye on in After is the arithmetic line ("`6 - 3 = 3` selects reply"), which is correct but reads oddly; phrasing it as "the three prior findings offset the menu, so displayed 6 is raw 3" keeps the echo clear. Nothing regressed, so no wording needs restoring from Before.
